1: # Floooww backend context
2: 
3: Floooww is a Django/DRF backend for a creator-management and brand-collaboration platform. Brands create campaigns; creators maintain professional profiles, discover and apply to campaigns, collaborate, receive payments, build ratings, and can be rehired. Admins approve and manage platform participants.
4: 
5: ## Current foundation
6: 
7: - Django 6, DRF, JWT, Channels, Celery, Redis, and SQLite for local development.
8: - API root: `/api/`; documentation: `/api/docs/`; health check: `/api/health/`.
9: - `users` provides shared accounts, roles, authentication, and approval. Role-specific business data belongs in dedicated profile modules.
10: - Notification email templates live in `apps/notifications/templates/notifications/emails/`.
11: - Local media uses `media/`. S3 is opt-in through `USE_S3=True` after AWS credentials, bucket policy, and deployment settings are ready.
12: - Local commands: `./scripts/start-dev.ps1`, `./scripts/stop-dev.ps1`, `./.venv/Scripts/python.exe manage.py test`, and `./.venv/Scripts/python.exe manage.py createsuperuser`.
13: - Organizations plus Brand, Agency, and Creator profile foundations are implemented. `apps/creator/social/` is the single runtime owner of creator social identities and snapshots.
14: - The canonical Campaign aggregate is implemented under `apps/brand/campaigns/`, including tenant-scoped CRUD, requirements, deliverable templates/reordering, commercial/tracking sections, protected lifecycle commands, activity history, filters, and pagination. `apps/agency/campaigns/` provides a thin Agency-scoped API over that aggregate with exact client delegation and cross-agency isolation. Agency campaign creation requires an `ONBOARDING` or `ACTIVE` client linked to a Brand organization. Paid publication stops at `PENDING_FUNDING` until the payment-provider phase supplies trusted funding confirmation.
15: - `apps/creator/opportunities/` implements the published marketplace, saved campaigns, explainable eligibility gates, creator-owned applications, immutable application status history, and Brand/Agency-scoped review/shortlist/reject/select commands. Match scores remain unavailable until weights are approved.
16: - `apps/brand/discovery/` owns direct Creator invitations. Brand/Agency campaign managers can create, list, and cancel them; Creators can list, view, accept, or decline their own invitations. Open invitations expire lazily, have a 1--30 day lifetime (default 7), and are unique per campaign/creator. Acceptance reserves capacity and atomically creates an `AWAITING_CREATOR` collaboration with copied deliverables, never a fabricated application. Paid invitations require trusted funding. In-app notifications and audit events are emitted after commit.
17: - `apps/collaborations/` implements atomic application selection, creator acceptance/decline, immutable collaboration status events, copied creator-specific deliverables, versioned submissions, Brand/Agency review actions, optional Agency-to-client review routing, scoped deliverable comments, and creator-owned manual live-post registration. `Campaign.client_review_required` defaults to false; the exact linked Brand workspace completes `CLIENT_REVIEW` when used. 1: # Social provider integration contract
2: 
3: ## Decision and scope
4: 
5: Floooww will integrate directly with the official developer APIs for YouTube,
6: TikTok, and Instagram. The first release does not use a metrics reseller.
7: Twitch remains a frontend/model vocabulary value but is outside this release.
8: Exact Instagram permissions and metric names must be frozen against the current
9: Meta app review requirements when the developer app is created.
10: 
11: This document is authoritative for provider ownership, OAuth, ingestion, and
12: metric provenance. The frontend demonstrates required presentation; it is not
13: an authoritative source for provider identity, connection state, or metrics.
14: 
15: ## Ownership boundary
16: 
17: - `integrations.ProviderConnection` owns OAuth state, encrypted access/refresh
18:   tokens, granted scopes, token expiry, provider errors, revocation, and sync
19:   health. Tokens are never stored in `.env` per creator and never serialized.
20: - `creator.social.SocialAccount` owns the creator-facing platform identity and
21:   latest safe metric summary. It links one-to-one to a provider connection when
22:   the integrations app is implemented; it does not own another token copy.
23: - `AudienceSnapshot` and `SocialMetricSnapshot` are immutable normalized
24:   provider observations. Raw values remain nullable when unavailable.
25: - Provider callbacks and privileged workers are the only writers of provider
26:   identity, scopes, connection state, metrics, and audience snapshots.
27: - Until adapters are implemented, public connect/sync actions return `503`.
28:   They must never fall back to accepting client-supplied handles or metrics.
29: 
30: The current `SocialAccount.connection_status` is a transitional local field.
31: When `ProviderConnection` is introduced, its status becomes authoritative and
32: the social serializer derives connection health from it.
33: 
34: ## Provider capability baseline
35: 
36: | Provider | Connection/API baseline | Initial requested access | Availability rule |
37: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
38: | YouTube | Google OAuth web-server flow, YouTube Data API, YouTube Analytics API | `youtube.readonly`, `yt-analytics.readonly`; monetary scope excluded initially | Channel/video metadata and owner-authorized analytics only. Service accounts are not used for creator analytics. |
39: | TikTok | Login Kit/OAuth plus Display API | `user.info.basic`, request `user.info.profile`, `user.info.stats`, and `video.list` only when required and approved | Do not promise reach, impressions, or audience demographics unless the approved API response supplies them. |
40: | Instagram | Meta developer app and Instagram API for professional Creator/Business accounts | Minimum identity/media/insights permissions approved for the selected login product | Exact scopes and metrics are versioned and frozen during app review; consumer accounts and unavailable metrics are reported explicitly. |
41: 
42: Official references:
43: 
44: - YouTube OAuth and Analytics: https://developers.google.com/youtube/reporting/guides/authorization
45: - YouTube Analytics API: https://developers.google.com/youtube/analytics/reference
46: - Google OAuth web-server flow: https://developers.google.com/youtube/data/guides/auth/server-side-web-apps
47: - TikTok scopes: https://developers.tiktok.com/docs/en/tiktok-api-scopes
48: - TikTok Display API: https://developers.tiktok.com/docs/en/display-api-get-started
49: - TikTok token lifecycle: https://developers.tiktok.com/docs/en/oauth-user-access-token-management
50: - Meta's official Instagram API collection: https://www.postman.com/meta/instagram/documentation/6yqw8pt/instagram-api
51: 
52: ## OAuth and lifecycle
53: 
54: 1. `POST /api/v1/integrations/{provider}/start/` validates creator ownership,
55:    creates short-lived single-use state, uses PKCE where supported, and returns
56:    the provider authorization URL.
57: 2. The callback validates state, exact redirect URI, provider response, and
58:    granted scopes before exchanging the authorization code server-side.
59: 3. The adapter fetches the provider subject/account identity. A transaction
60:    upserts `ProviderConnection` and the linked `SocialAccount`; the browser
61:    cannot choose `external_account_id`.
62: 4. Token refresh and scheduled sync run in Celery with provider-specific rate
63:    limits, bounded exponential backoff, jitter, and non-secret error logging.
64: 5. Disconnect attempts provider revocation, marks the connection revoked even
65:    if the provider is unavailable, stops future jobs, and retains previously
66:    authorized snapshots according to the retention policy.
67: 6. Webhooks are signature-verified, idempotent, stored with a provider event
68:    identifier, and processed asynchronously.
69: 
70: ## Metric normalization and provenance
71: 
72: Every adapter maps provider fields into a versioned normalized schema. Store
73: the provider, external subject, reporting window, capture time, API/version,
74: and a non-secret response/job reference. Never translate missing, unsupported,
75: permission-denied, or not-yet-synced values into zero. Responses expose an
76: availability reason such as `available`, `unsupported`, `permission_required`,
77: `account_ineligible`, `not_synced`, or `provider_error`.
78: 
79: Follower/subscriber count and engagement rate are nullable summaries. Derived
80: engagement must record its formula and inputs in adapter metadata; do not assume
81: one formula across platforms. Audience demographics require explicit creator
82: consent and the approved provider capability. Public creator serializers expose
83: only safe summaries and must honor profile privacy flags.
84: 
85: ## Configuration and rollout gate
86: 
87: Developer application credentials are server-only:
88: 
89: - `YOUTUBE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `YOUTUBE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `YOUTUBE_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`
90: - `TIKTOK_CLIENT_KEY`, `TIKTOK_CLIENT_SECRET`, `TIKTOK_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`
91: - `INSTAGRAM_APP_ID`, `INSTAGRAM_APP_SECRET`, `INSTAGRAM_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`
92: - `SOCIAL_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `SOCIAL_SYNC_ENABLED`, `SOCIAL_SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES`
93: 
94: `SOCIAL_SYNC_ENABLED` stays false until credentials, redirect URIs, app review,
95: token encryption, revocation, mocked adapter tests, and one sandbox end-to-end
96: test per provider pass. Unit and ordinary API tests never make live provider
97: requests; adapters use fixtures and mocked HTTP responses.
98: 
99: ## Implementation checklist
100: 
101: 1. Build `integrations.ProviderConnection`, OAuth state, encrypted credential
102:    storage, provider-event/idempotency records, and adapter interfaces.
103: 2. Implement YouTube, then TikTok, then Instagram behind separate feature flags.
104: 3. Add start/callback/reconnect/revoke endpoints and Celery refresh/sync jobs.
105: 4. Link canonical `creator.social.SocialAccount`; do not create another social
106:    account model in profiles or provider apps.
107: 5. Add capability/availability fields and provider provenance to snapshots.
108: 6. Add permission, cross-creator isolation, replay, expired-state, refresh,
109:    rate-limit, partial-data, revocation, and privacy tests.
110: 7. Update frontend empty/error/reconnect states before enabling each provider.
